page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an entry-level x86_64 virtual machine belonging to the N1 server family. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.9 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include any bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of cloud compute resources. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1086.39, while the multi-core score reaches 1408.88. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.82 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 13.22 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 1638.85 and 730.43 respectively, reflecting entry-level processing capabilities.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-2 is its constrained memory capacity of 2.0 GB, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. However, because it utilizes dedicated vCPUs rather than shared-core resources, it provides predictable, albeit modest, compute performance. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for lightweight, compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints.

This instance is suited for lightweight utility workloads, simple background workers, basic static web serving, and small-scale single-threaded tasks such as basic file compression or low-volume text processing.
